name: Gilt market
summary: 10-year gilt near 5.18% on 10 Nov as BoE signals another rate rise; yields near 19-year highs, no weak auction found
state: The 10-year gilt yield rose to about 5.18% on 10 Nov, tracking US Treasuries after hot US inflation data, as Deputy Governor Lombardelli said another near-term Bank of England rise was likely (Trading Economics). Yields remain near their highest since 2007 after the 5 Nov rate rise to 4% (Bank of England). No weak auction or BoE intervention was found as of 11 Nov, so Watch is kept.
for_you: High gilt yields feed through to fixed mortgage rates and annuity pricing, and raise the government's borrowing costs. Mortgage deals tend to reprice within weeks of moves in gilt yields.
rubric_hit: Gilt yields at multi-decade highs: Watch; no BoE intervention or 10y move > 75bp in a month

sources.title: Trading Economics — UK Bond Yields Edge Up
Bank of England — November 2026 Monetary Policy Report

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
